questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Qatar?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Qatar article.

questions.proof: The Capital of Qatar is Doha, where over 90% of the people.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Qatar?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Qatar on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Qatar article.

questions.proof: A strait in the Persian Gulf separates Qatar from the nearby island country of Bahrain, as well as sharing maritime borders with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Iran.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Qatar?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “People and culture” part of the Qatar article.

questions.proof: The official language of Qatar is Arabic, but many people also speak English, especially when they are doing business.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Qatar?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “People and culture” part of the Qatar article.

questions.proof: The Currency of Qatar is called Qatari Riyal or Riyal.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 2014, Qatar's relations with _____, Saudi Arabia and United Arab Emirates (UAE) came to a boiling point over Qatar's support for the Muslim Brotherhood and extremist groups in Syria.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Saudi”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Qatar article, under the heading “Foreign relations”.

questions.proof: Between 1760 and 1971, Qatar sought formal protection from the high transitory powers of the Ottomans, British, the Al-Khalifa's from Bahrain, the Arabians, and the Wahhabis from Saudi Arabia.
